gaps.parameter: end-cap cone geometry (height, base diameter, apex/antenna bore)
gaps.issue: cones appear in Fig. 1(a,e) only, no dimensions. They DOMINATE Q_Cu: with flat ends at the stated dims (R_s = 4.83 mOhm) the end plates carry 77-78% of the Cu loss and Q_Cu = 2.7e6 vs 1.10e7 in Tab I/II; the side wall alone gives Q ~1.2e7 (x0.84 -> ~1.03e7). The cones (which pull the field off the end plates) are what makes the paper's end-cap share only 16%. Earlier claim 'cone sensitivity small' was wrong for Q_Cu/G.
gaps.proposal: Q_Cu/G is a cone-dominated, UNRELIABLE 2D target while the cone geometry is unknown; use it only as a cone-calibration quantity (or compare the side-wall-only Q ~1.2e7). 2D hard targets: Delta f(eps), Delta f(T), p_e, C trend. Baseline: copy the sister design 2004.02754 (Fig. 4/Fig. 10: cone height 6 mm, base diameter = inner-tube inner diameter, ~4 mm antenna bore); sweep height 0 (flat) .. 10 mm and base diameter 20.7..21.75 mm; report f, C030, G sensitivity. Hint: V = 1.0776 L with D = 57.1 mm leaves ~2.1 cm^3 for two cones, i.e. ~8 mm tall cones of base radius ~10.9 mm (inferred, UNVERIFIED).

Sweep the tube end gap 0-1.5 mm (each end) as a parameter. Tubes touching both endplates is physically doubtful: the inner tube is the one reused in 2410.07774 where L_Al2O3 = 420 mm at 300 K in a 422.23 mm body, and differential contraction (Cu ~0.33% vs sapphire ~0.08%) requires a gap; 2410 shows a 0.73 mm gap moves C from ~0.34 (no gap) to 0.235. Pins ignored (paper: negligible loss).

gaps.issue: Table I/II use thermally rescaled dimensions, coefficients not printed (only 'refs 45, 46')
gaps.proposal: use integrated contraction 293->4 K: Cu -3.26e-3, sapphire ~ -8e-4 (literature, UNVERIFIED for this paper); the paper attributes 9 MHz to geometry, so the sensitivity is small; reproduce Table II first with RT geometry and with contracted geometry
use 57.1 (drawing; also closer to the quoted V)
use scalar eps (paper's model); optionally eps_par = eps (axial), eps_perp ~ 9.3 as a sensitivity check

inconsistencies.description: Table I column header 'sigma_eff_Cu' (no unit) holds 1/R_s in siemens, not a conductivity
inconsistencies.evidence: 1/207.04 = 4.83e-3 Ohm = 'surface copper resistivity 0.00483 Ohm' (text p.4); 1/37.75 Ohm <=> sigma = 5.88e7 S/m (RT copper). Q_Cu scales linearly with this column (QCu*Rs constant), as it must for 1/R_s.
inconsistencies.proposal: use R_s = 1/column. NOTE 2410.07774 later used '5.48x RT conductivity' (=207.04/37.75) as a sigma ratio, which is the 1/R_s ratio - see quax_clamshell_2410.json

inconsistencies.description: Q_Sapph at 4.2 K (1.03e9) is inconsistent with all other rows
inconsistencies.evidence: p_e = 1/(Q_Sapph tan_delta) = 0.170 for T = 293..25 K but 0.816 at 4.2 K; with p_e = 0.170, tan_delta = 1.19e-9 gives Q_Sapph = 4.94e9, i.e. the Table II eps=11.3/11.44 values (4.96e9, 4.98e9). Table II eps=11.1 row (1.21e9) is likewise off.
inconsistencies.proposal: benchmark p_e (= 0.170) and Q_Cu (G ~ 5.3e4 Ohm) separately; treat printed Q_Sapph(4.2 K)=1.03e9 and Q0(4.2 K)=1.08e7 as possibly affected (Q0 would be 1.098e7 with Q_Sapph = 4.94e9); text quotes 'as high as 11e6'
compare Q_Cu and f, C030 only for that row

inconsistencies.description: Table I Q0 slightly below 1/(1/Q_Cu+1/Q_Sapph) at low T (1-2%: 77 K 5.88e6 vs 5.95e6, 50 K 9.02e6 vs 9.18e6, 25 K 1.06e7 vs 1.08e7)
inconsistencies.proposal: tolerance of ~2% on Q0 comparisons; Q0 probably from a separate combined-loss run

inconsistencies.description: Simulated f is 121 MHz (1.2%) above measured at 4 K
inconsistencies.evidence: Fig. 3 caption: 'simulation frequencies shifted by 121 MHz'; conclusions claim agreement within ~1%
inconsistencies.proposal: benchmark against simulated f (Table I/II), measurement only as sanity check

inconsistencies.description: the earlier literature survey lists 'cone dimensions UNVERIFIED' - confirmed: no cone dimension in 2201.04223

Absolute f and C are not reproduced by an exact z-invariant layered-cylinder TM0n0 model at the stated dims (4.2 K, eps 11.2, Cu -3.26e-3 / sapphire -8e-4 contraction, flat ends): f = 10.364 GHz, C = 0.0378, p_e = 0.170 vs Tab II 10.4745 GHz, 0.0321, (p_e 0.170). Cone shift scaled from 2004.02754 ~ +14 MHz leaves ~95 MHz (0.9%) unexplained. Differences DO reproduce: eps 11.44->11.2 shift 18.5 MHz (paper 19), thermal 8.8 MHz (paper 9), p_e 0.170 exact. df/dR1 ~ -0.66 GHz/mm: R1 = 10.73 mm (within the +-0.15 mm ID tolerance) gives ~10.45-10.46 GHz.
inconsistencies.evidence: f/C/p_e re-run independently (10.3640 GHz, 0.0378, 0.170; flat-end Q_Cu 2.74e6, end share 77%, side-wall-only Q 1.21e7)
inconsistencies.proposal: hard targets = Delta f(eps), Delta f(T), p_e, C trend vs eps/T; absolute f tolerance ~1%, absolute C ~15% (or fit R1 / end gap first and then compare); Q_Cu only with a fitted cone

inconsistencies.description: Table II eps = 11.2 row Q_Cu = 1.09e7 vs Table I 4.2 K row Q_Cu = 1.10e7 for the same conditions (4.2 K geometry, eps 11.2, R_s 4.83 mOhm)
inconsistencies.proposal: 1% tolerance; Q_Cu is a soft target anyway (cone-dominated)

solver_class.reason: Coaxial tubes, cylinder and on-axis cones are axisymmetric; pseudo-TM030 is m=0. Teflon pins and the sapphire tuning rods (absent in Table I/II) break symmetry but the paper says pin loss is negligible. Mode crossings with TE/TEM modes (seen in measurement) would need m!=0 / 3D. Also omitted in 2D: teflon pins (harmless for TM0n0: axial currents).

priority_reason: Tabulated f, C030, Q_Cu, Q_Sapph vs eps and T for a 2D-axisymmetric dielectric-loaded cavity. Cone and tube-end-gap geometry are missing. Q_Cu/G is cone-dominated (flat ends give 2.7e6 vs 1.1e7) -> unreliable target; absolute f is ~0.9% and C ~15% off an exact model at stated dims. Good targets: Delta f(eps), Delta f(T), p_e = 0.170, C trends.

readme_row.quantities: hard: Delta f(eps), Delta f(T), p_e; soft: absolute f (~1%), C030 (~15%); Q_Cu cone-dominated (unreliable)
